newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five prison guards killed in Colombia riot.
newsitem.headline: Five prison guards killed in Colombia riot.

text.p: Inmates killed at least five prison guards and took 15 hostages during a riot at a jail in northern Colombia on Thursday, prison authorities said.

The prisoners were armed and in control of the jail compound, officials said. At least five of the jail's 500 inmates were injured in a shoot-out before they managed to strip the guards of their pistols and night sticks.
Police and soldiers surrounded the prison in Valledupar, in Cesar province, and fired bullets and tear gas over the walls but were unable to enter.

"A prisoner has reported that five guards are dead and they are holding 15 hostages. The inmates have seized the guards' weapons and the situation is still not under control," a spokeswoman of the National Prisons' Institute INPEC said. The deputy prison director, guards and administrative staff were among the hostages, the spokeswoman said.

"The dead and injured are inside the jail and the problems are still continuing. The shooting has died down but the inmates have taken over the jail," a police spokesman told Reuters by phone from Valledupar.

The prisoners, who include a number of convicted leftist guerrillas, called for ambulances, doctors, international Red Cross officials and the local human rights' ombudsman to go to the jail before they would negotiate an end to the crisis.
Their demands included an end to overcrowding and better health conditions, the prison spokeswoman said.

The latest incident is the worst in a string of prison disturbances this year. Last week, more than 2,000 inmates, led by leftist guerrillas, rioted and started fires in Bogota's La Modelo jail in protest at prison overcrowding.

Another convict died in the top-security wing of Bogota's La Picota jail when a bomb he was making in his cell accidentally exploded. Prisoners have rioted in at least three provincial jails so far this year to press for better conditions.
